edges.description: Failure to regenerate 11-cis-retinol from all-trans-retinyl esters prevents supply of the photopigment chromophore 11-cis-retinal to rod and cone photoreceptors, arresting the visual cycle.

Rod photoreceptors depend entirely on the RPE65-dependent visual cycle for 11-cis-retinal, so chromophore depletion silences rod phototransduction before any photoreceptor is lost. This is the functional, pre-degenerative step that produces night blindness from the first year of life, and it is why rescuing the enzyme can restore light sensitivity in a retina that is structurally still present.

Loss of the rod-driven component of the afferent pupillary pathway follows from the same chromophore starvation; pupils in LCA2 are poorly reactive or frankly amaurotic in infancy, which is one of the findings that brings an affected infant to ophthalmological attention.

Chronic 11-cis-retinal depletion produces ongoing rod and cone metabolic stress and drives progressive photoreceptor loss, starting with rod-dominant degeneration that eventually extends to cone loss and outer retinal atrophy.
Rod photoreceptors are densest outside the macula, so rod-dominant degeneration removes peripheral retinal sensitivity first and the visual field constricts progressively toward fixation.

Photophobia appears as cone degeneration advances in the mid-stage of the rod-cone dystrophy, rather than at presentation. It is a variable feature and is recorded here as a mid-stage consequence of degeneration, not as an early diagnostic sign.
Progressive rod then cone loss produces night blindness, peripheral field constriction, and ultimately loss of central vision; most LCA2 individuals are legally blind by the fourth decade.

Emmetropisation - the visually driven reduction of refractive error over infancy and early childhood - depends on retinal image quality, so an eye that receives almost no usable visual input in the first years fails to emmetropise and remains highly hyperopic.

Nystagmus in LCA2 is a consequence of profound visual deprivation during the critical period for fixation development, not an independent oculomotor lesion. Its severity tracks the amount of residual central vision, so it is prominent in infantile-onset LCA2 and mild or absent where cone-mediated vision is preserved.
The reduced rod and cone ERG responses measure the panretinal visual-cycle defect impairing phototransduction.

nodes.description: Electroretinography typically shows markedly reduced or absent rod responses on dark-adapted testing and impaired cone responses on light-adapted testing, consistent with the panretinal visual cycle defect affecting both rod and cone photoreceptors.

evidence.snippet: Electroretinogram examination shows an attenuated visual response in the cone cells and a complete loss of visual response under scotopic, dark-adapted conditions

reports_on.interpretation: The reduced rod and cone ERG responses measure the panretinal visual-cycle defect impairing phototransduction.

nodes.description: Pupillary responses are sluggish or absent (amaurotic pupils) from infancy, reflecting loss of the photoreceptor-driven afferent limb of the light reflex. In a young infant this is one of the few objective bedside signs of the profound retinal dysfunction, since acuity cannot yet be measured.

evidence.snippet: characterised clinically by severe congenital/early infancy visual loss, nystagmus, amaurotic pupils and markedly reduced/absent full-field electroretinograms

nodes.description: Infants with LCA frequently have high hyperopia, attributed to failure of the visually driven emmetropisation that normally reduces refractive error over the first years of life. It matters clinically because it is detectable at the first examination and because uncorrected high refractive error compounds the visual deficit in a child whose remaining function is worth preserving.

evidence.snippet: Affected infants often have high hyperopia, or less commonly high myopia, suggesting impaired emmetropisation.

nodes.description: Night blindness is commonly the first symptom, often apparent in infancy or early childhood in the LCA2/EOSRD forms, reflecting the rod-dominant initial functional deficit from 11-cis-retinal depletion.

evidence.snippet: Individuals typically experience progressive decline in central vision, and many meet the criteria for legal blindness by the fourth decade; some progress to profound visual loss (including no light perception) by mid-adulthood. In RPE65-related juvenile RP, onset of visual manifestations typically occurs in late childhood or adolescence. Individuals often present with nyctalopia, progressive peripheral visual field loss, and relatively preserved central visual acuity in earlier stages.

evidence.snippet: early-onset severe nyctalopia, nystagmus, low vision, and progressive visual field constriction, with retinitis pigmentosa by other genetic mutations, appropriate genetic testing is essential to make a correct diagnosis

nodes.description: Nystagmus reflects early and severe impairment of visual function from infancy and may be the first sign prompting ophthalmological evaluation. Its frequency within RPE65-related disease should not be overstated: it is characteristic of the infantile-onset LCA2 end of the spectrum, whereas most children with biallelic RPE65 variants have an EOSRD phenotype with residual cone-mediated vision and mild or absent nystagmus.

evidence.snippet: A less common but more severe inherited retinal dystrophy, Leber congenital amaurosis, a retinitis pigmentosa subtype, is further characterised by earlier onset, more rapid progression, and nystagmus.

evidence.snippet: Most children with RPE65 deficiency have an EOSRD phenotype with profound night blindness from birth but residual cone-mediated vision and often mild if any nystagmus.

nodes.description: Light sensitivity/photoaversion is a variable feature of the retinal dystrophy spectrum that includes RPE65-associated disease, most often reported in the mid-stage of rod-cone degeneration. It is a less consistent feature than nyctalopia and visual field constriction in RPE65-related retinopathy, and its reported frequency varies across cohorts.

evidence.snippet: patients may become photophobic, especially in response to diffuse light, such as occurs with cloudy weather

evidence.reference_title: RPE65-Associated Retinopathies in the Italian Population: A Longitudinal Natural History Study.

nodes.description: Chronic visual cycle arrest drives progressive rod photoreceptor apoptosis followed by secondary cone degeneration and outer retinal atrophy. The slow rate of degeneration reflects the ability of photoreceptors to survive for years or decades without adequate 11-cis-retinal, but the trajectory is inexorably toward complete blindness without intervention. Gene therapy can interrupt this cascade by restoring enzymatic activity in residual viable RPE.

evidence.snippet: despite the absence of functional RPE65 isomerohydrolase and the subsequent inability of the retinal pigment epithelium cells to provide sufficient 11-cis retinal to the photoreceptors, the photoreceptors degenerate slowly, so that phenotypic recovery is possible through restoration of the missing enzyme to the retinal pigment epithelium cells.

while vision is relatively stable in the first decade of life, it begins to decline again starting in the teens, with 50% of individuals being legally blind (visual acuity of 20/200 and/or visual fields extending <20 degrees from fixation) by age 20 years.

nodes.description: Constriction of the peripheral visual field accompanies rod degeneration and is progressive; severe constriction is present by early adulthood in most LCA2/EOSRD patients.

evidence.snippet: Mean sum total degrees of Goldmann visual field (III4e) nearly doubled in the intervention group and decreased in the control group

nodes.description: Pathogenic variants in RPE65 reduce or abolish the enzymatic activity of all-trans-retinyl ester isomerohydrolase in RPE cells. RPE65 normally catalyzes the conversion of all-trans-retinyl esters to 11-cis-retinol in the retinoid (visual) cycle; loss of this activity depletes the supply of 11-cis-retinal available for photopigment regeneration in adjacent rod and cone photoreceptors. The RPE cell is the primary site of defect; photoreceptors themselves do not express RPE65.

evidence.snippet: The RPE65 gene encodes all-trans retinyl ester isomerase, an enzyme crucial to the retinoid cycle.
Within the RPE cells, stored all-trans retinal is isomerized to 11-cis retinal by retinal pigment epithelial 65-kDa (RPE65) protein.

The diagnosis of autosomal recessive RPE65-related retinal degeneration is established in a proband with suggestive findings and biallelic pathogenic variants in RPE65 identified by molecular genetic testing.

nodes.description: Visual acuity is typically severely impaired from early life in LCA2/EOSRD and progressively declines to legal blindness in the second to fourth decade.

evidence.snippet: children ages four to ten years in the largest case series had severe visual impairment (mean visual acuity: 20/126).

nodes.description: Absent or severely reduced RPE65 activity arrests the retinoid cycle at the all-trans-retinyl ester stage, preventing regeneration of 11-cis-retinol and ultimately 11-cis-retinal. Without this chromophore, opsin proteins in rod and cone outer segments remain in an unliganded (apo-opsin) state. Apo-opsin cannot form functional photopigment and may signal constitutively, generating abnormal phototransduction cascade activity and metabolic stress in photoreceptor cells.

evidence.snippet: The three phenotypes of autosomal recessive RPE65-related retinal degeneration, from most severe to mildest, are Leber congenital amaurosis (LCA), early-onset severe retinal dystrophy (EOSRD), and juvenile retinitis pigmentosa (RP).

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of voretigene neparvovec (AAV2-hRPE65v2) in patients with RPE65-mediated inherited retinal dystrophy: a randomised, controlled, open-label, phase 3 trial.
evidence.snippet: Biallelic mutations in this gene, which disrupt the visual cyde, can be described as Leber congenital amaurosis type 2, retinitis pigmentosa type 20, early-onset retinal dystrophy, and other clinical labels for severe rod-mediated inherited retinal dystrophies, which all eventually progress to complete blindness.
